log.briefing:
Market briefing for 13 Nov 2026 (current holdings: all cash)

Note: My search tool hit its usage limit partway through. Gold, emerging markets, geopolitics and the dates of upcoming events are not confirmed here and need to be checked separately.

Last two weeks
- Fed and rates: Markets now expect the Fed to raise rates again. On 10–11 Nov, CME FedWatch put the chance of a 0.25-point hike at the December meeting at about 87–90% (Yahoo Finance, CNBC). Goldman Sachs now expects hikes in both December and March. Fed Governor Waller raised the possibility of a 0.5-point hike if inflation stays high, and Dallas Fed President Logan said at least two more hikes may be needed. Williams and Daly also favour more hikes but at a slower pace. According to TheStreet (13 Nov), all 10 Fed officials who have spoken since the 5 Nov selloff lean toward more hikes.
- Inflation (BLS, 10 Nov): Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than expected. Excluding food and energy, they rose 0.3%. Because data collection lapsed in October 2025, BLS could not publish many 12-month figures.
- Jobs (BLS, 6 Nov): Employers added 165,000 jobs in October against forecasts of about 60,000. Unemployment fell to 4.1% and hourly pay rose 0.4% on the month. Long-term unemployment, however, is the highest outside the pandemic in a decade (CNBC).
- Treasuries (TLT, IEF): Prices fell. On 12 Nov the 10-year yield rose more than 0.13 points to about 5.13%, the 30-year to about 5.45% and the 2-year to about 4.88% (CNBC). Rising oil prices and expected hikes drove the move. TheStreet also reported weak demand at a Treasury auction on 12 Nov.
- Nvidia (QQQ, SPY): On 12 Nov the company said Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO with immediate effect, amid scandals reported by CNN and Yahoo Finance. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and Harvey Jones is the first board chair. The shares fell, and several brokers downgraded the stock that week.
- Stocks: On 10 Nov the S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,520.93 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.7%. The Nasdaq then slid again on 12 Nov after the Nvidia news.
- Sentiment: The share of bearish investors in the AAII survey went above 50% for the first time in eight weeks. Professional investors' stock exposure is at an eight-week low, and the VIX fear index was about 19.5 on 10 Nov. Weekly jobless claims (4-week average) are at their lowest since 1969.
- Oil and geopolitics: Oil rose on 12 Nov. I could not confirm the cause.

Next two weeks
- 13 Nov: Producer price inflation (PPI) for October, plus four Fed speakers (TheStreet).
- Watch for: more Fed speeches before the December meeting, Nvidia's quarterly results and new Treasury auctions. Dates are not confirmed.
- December Fed meeting: a hike is mostly priced in. The exact date is not confirmed here.

Not covered (search limit)
- Gold (GLD): no current price or news.
- Emerging and developed markets outside the US (EEM, EFA): no news. Higher US yields usually weigh on both, but this is a general pattern, not a sourced finding.

Facts only, not investment advice.

Sources: BLS (bls.gov/cpi), CNBC (10–12 Nov), Yahoo Finance (11–12 Nov), TheStreet Pro (12–13 Nov), CNN (12 Nov), NVIDIA newsroom, Babypips and ANI (6 Nov).

The goal is to beat SPY after costs, and the 50% per-ETF cap rules out holding SPY alone, so I hold SPY at the maximum and fill most of the rest with QQQ and EFA, keeping the order count low. EFA is the lower-volatility complement, and QQQ is kept smaller because of the Nvidia CEO turmoil and its 35% volatility. I avoid bonds (yields rising into a likely December hike), gold (steep downtrend) and EEM and IWM (weak and sensitive to rates), and set a long review interval to limit fees.
